data.name: Diandra
data.gender_notes: Diandra is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Greek mythology, Diandra was the goddess of the moon and the hunt. Her name is derived from the Greek words 'dia' meaning 'through' and 'andra' meaning 'man' or 'moon'. In Christian tradition, Diandra represents the divine feminine and the wisdom of the moon. The name Diandra carries the meaning “Goddess of the Moon” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Diandra usually hope their child will grow to embody goddess of the moon and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbol of divine feminine wisdom and the cycles of life.
data.etymology: Diandra belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Goddess of the Moon.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Diandra total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

in_greek.name: Διανδρά
in_greek.long_meaning: Διανδρά (Δία + άνδρα) είναι μια ελληνική-λατινική المرأة اسم, που συνίσταται από Δία (Δία, θεά της φύσης) και άνδρα (άνδρα, άντρας). signification: 'Strong woman, ruler' ή 'natural princess'.

in_latin.name: Diandra
in_latin.long_meaning: Diandra est nomen femininum quod ex Diana (dea naturae) et Andra (vir) compositum est. Significatio: 'mulier fortis, domina' seu 'principis naturales'.

in_english.name: Diandra
in_english.meaning: Strong woman, ruler, natural princess, feminine and powerful
in_english.long_meaning: Diandra is a feminine given name derived from the Latin words Diana, meaning 'goddess of nature', and Andra, meaning 'woman' or 'strong one'. In Christian tradition, Diandra is associated with qualities of strength, courage, and leadership. It is a popular name among Christians, particularly in cultures with Latin American and European influences.
